name: Estuary / delta
notes: Brackish tidal river mouths and deltas: cordgrass and glasswort marsh fringing mudflats, reed and bulrush beds on the fresher side, mangrove in tropical deltas, and eelgrass in the channels. Drawn on Atlantic North America (Chesapeake), NW Europe (Wadden Sea, Thames), the Mekong/Ganges deltas and SE Australian estuaries; underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Grey mangrove
canopy.source: Avicennia marina, Indo-West Pacific and E Africa estuaries, most cold-tolerant mangrove with pencil roots, 3-14 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Nipa palm
canopy.source: Nypa fruticans, SE Asian and Bay of Bengal deltas (Mekong, Sundarbans), trunkless palm in brackish tidal mud, 4-9 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Swamp she-oak
canopy.source: Casuarina glauca, E Australian estuary margins behind mangroves, needle-like branchlets, 8-20 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Crack willow
canopy.source: Salix fragilis (S. x fragilis), European tidal river banks and freshwater deltas, 10-20 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Sea purslane shrub
shrub.source: Halimione (Atriplex) portulacoides, European Atlantic and Mediterranean estuary creek banks, silver-grey subshrub 30-80 cm — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Marsh elder
shrub.source: Iva frutescens, US Atlantic/Gulf estuary high-marsh edge, shrub 1-3 m — USDA Plants

shrub.name: Groundsel bush
shrub.source: Baccharis halimifolia, SE US and Gulf estuary margins (invasive in Australia/Europe), fluffy white seed heads, 1-4 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Smooth cordgrass
ground.source: Sporobolus (Spartina) alterniflorus, US Atlantic/Gulf low marsh (invasive in China/W Europe), daily-flooded cordgrass 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Common cordgrass
ground.source: Sporobolus (Spartina) anglicus, NW European estuary mudflats (hybrid origin, Southampton), pioneer cordgrass 0.3-1.3 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Common reed
ground.source: Phragmites australis, cosmopolitan, brackish upper estuary and delta reedbeds (Danube, Rhone), 2-4 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Glasswort
ground.source: Salicornia europaea, N Hemisphere estuary mudflat pioneer, jointed succulent annual turning red in autumn, 5-30 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Saltmarsh bulrush
ground.source: Bolboschoenus maritimus, near-cosmopolitan brackish estuary margins and delta ponds, triangular-stemmed sedge 0.5-1.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sea aster
ground.source: Tripolium pannonicum (Aster tripolium), European estuary marsh, fleshy-leaved lilac daisy 20-80 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Eelgrass
ground.source: underwater — Zostera marina, N Hemisphere estuary and lagoon channels on sand/mud, ribbon-leaved seagrass 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Widgeongrass
ground.source: underwater — Ruppia maritima, worldwide brackish estuary shallows, thread-leaved submerged plant 20-80 cm — Wikipedia
